findings.title: Group membership removal passes an id to `users.delete`, which expects a record
Pagination math is wrong at page boundaries
Public members endpoint has no upper bound on `limit` and no handling of negative values
Add-members flow lacks a save-first check and input clearing, and the member list can go stale
`findMembers` returns undefined when the name is empty, and `create`/`update` ignore errors

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Group membership removal passes an id to `users.delete`, which expects a record

Affected:
- app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:84-97

Explanation:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` is called with an integer. In Rails 4 a has_many through `delete` expects model records. An integer may raise `AssociationTypeMismatch` or be treated unreliably. With a through association it may also fail to remove the join row correctly. Look the user up first, or delete the GroupUser rows directly.

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
user = User.find_by(id: user_id)
group.users.delete(user) if user
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Pagination math is wrong at page boundaries

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:6-17

Explanation:
`totalPages` is computed as `floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (for example 50 members and a limit of 50), this reports 2 pages and the last page is empty. The `next` action then moves to an empty page, and `showingLast` is never true on the real last page. Use `Math.ceil`. The `next` action also clamps the offset to `user_count`, which can land on an empty page.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
return Math.ceil(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit"));
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Public members endpoint has no upper bound on `limit` and no handling of negative values

Affected:
- app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26

Explanation:
`limit` comes straight from user input. A huge value dumps the whole group, which undermines the pagination. A negative value or a negative offset can raise a DB error (500) or return unexpected results. The previous code capped the limit for automatic groups. Clamp both values (for example `limit` between 1 and 200, `offset` at least 0).

Proposed fix:
~~~ruby
limit = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 200].min
offset = [params[:offset].to_i, 0].max
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Add-members flow lacks a save-first check and input clearing, and the member list can go stale

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23-38

Explanation:
`usernames` is never cleared after adding (there is a TODO), so a second click re-adds the same users. `findMembers` clamps the offset to `user_count`. After removing the last member of the last page, the offset can point past the end and show an empty list, because it is not recalculated.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
var self = this;
this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames")).then(function(){ self.set("usernames", ""); });
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: `findMembers` returns undefined when the name is empty, and `create`/`update` ignore errors

Affected:
- app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20-22
- app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22-35

Explanation:
`findMembers` now returns undefined instead of a promise, which breaks callers that chain `.then`. In `create`, the group name is read from `params[:name]`, but `update` has no guard on the `alias_level` value.

Proposed fix:
~~~js
if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return Ember.RSVP.resolve(); }
~~~

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
